title: In 773 Arabidopsis thaliana accessions, each doubling of 45S rDNA copy number goes with about 2-3% less CHG DNA methylation across the genome; the link is observational and its direction is unresolved
abstract: Arabidopsis thaliana accessions that carry more copies of the 45S ribosomal RNA genes (rDNA) have slightly less CHG DNA methylation on transposons, genes and intergenic DNA across the genome. This matters because it is a population-scale plant test of the idea that large repeat arrays change gene silencing elsewhere by using up a limited pool of silencing proteins (the heterochromatin sink), an idea with experimental support in yeast and fruit flies but no test in plant populations. I counted rDNA copies with exact 25-base probes in short reads of 1,130 accessions of the 1001 Genomes collection and compared them with leaf methylomes of 773 accessions, in a mixed model that controls for genetic relatedness and methylome batch. Each doubling of rDNA went with 2.8% less CHG methylation of pericentromeric transposons (95% CI 1.5-4.1%; Bonferroni-corrected p = 7e-4 among 12 pre-registered tests; 3.5% in the pre-registered model, which had no batch term; 2.0%, CI 0.7-3.3%, when the three methylome batches are fitted separately and pooled). CHG methylation fell by 2.7-4.2% per doubling in all transposon groups, in gene bodies and in intergenic DNA; CG methylation changed little. The result held with control for DNA sequencing centre, geography and flowering time, with GC-corrected copy number, and with one accession per group of near-identical lines; all 12 rDNA probes alone gave negative estimates. It was clear in the largest methylome batch (585 accessions) but absent in a batch of 97. It is about one quarter of the change that full titration by rDNA base pairs predicts, and rDNA explains about 2% of the variation. The direction of cause is unresolved: natural alleles that change CHG methylation did not detectably change rDNA, but this test cannot exclude reverse causation, and the estimate within groups of closely related accessions agreed but was imprecise. Transposon expression did not change, but it also did not change with natural alleles of similar CHG effect, so this null is not informative. Probes for centromeric and 5S satellites counted sequence variants, not array size, and a genome-size association with flowering time disappeared after control for sequencing centre. Terms: CHG is a cytosine followed by any base and then G. If rDNA dosage is causal, existing Arabidopsis lines with 90% fewer rDNA copies should have about 7-10% more CHG methylation.

display.caption: The 12 pre-registered tests in 773 accessions, from the model with methylome batch: change in transposon methylation per doubling of copy number (kinship mixed model, 95% CI; filled = Bonferroni p < 0.05) and the change that full titration by repeat base pairs predicts (orange diamonds). Only rDNA is measured well; the CEN178 and 5S probes count sequence variants and the TE index counts Col-0 fragments.

(a) rDNA copy number and pericentromeric TE CHG methylation after removal of covariates and 10 kinship principal components (display only; line = mixed-model estimate; dashed = full titration). (b) Change in methylation per doubling of rDNA in each genome category and cytosine context: CHG falls in every category, CG changes little.

Read-based copy number (exact 25-mer probe counts in SRA reads) against the Fiscus & Koenig (2026) 12-mer index: the two agree for rDNA (Spearman 0.79; the index is compressed at high copy number) but not for CEN178 (0.02), where neither measure is validated.
